text:
Adam Fox has 23 points in 21 games, 21 of them assists, and the Rangers have needed every one with Sean Durzi out and Fox now playing almost 25 minutes a night. The Norris winner from 2020-21 has been the engine of a team that's won the chance battle in five straight games: with Fox on the ice at five on five, New York takes 60% of the expected goals (the quality of chances), more than 10 points better than without him.

If anything, his numbers are underselling him. The Rangers have scored 6.2 fewer goals than their chances deserve with him on the ice, which has cost him points, and that usually swings back. He has two goals on 3.4 expected, so even his own shooting has room to rise. Our talent range projects about 84 points.

Evolving-Hockey had him 9th among defensemen in wins above replacement last season, with 99th-percentile play-driving after adjusting for teammates and competition. The Hockey News, the New York Times and Newsday have all been making the same case lately: he's one of the best defensemen in the league, and this is what it looks like when he gets the minutes to show it.
